text:
alex: heads-up: noticed a parsing error in the browser sampleapp when users do very fast reconnects (~50ms). client logs show we got [DONE], then another data line with a partial json that breaks the parser. anyone seen this pattern before?

tara: can you paste the exact payload sequence?

alex: sure, snippet from dev proxy capture: 
```
data: {"chunk_id":1,"text":"first"}
data: {"chunk_id":2,"text":"second"}
data: [DONE]
data: {"chunk_id":2,"text":"!"}
```

omar: that implies the proxy is replaying a buffered packet after the server already sent the final event. iirc we changed keepalive/tcp_nodelay flags recently.

nina: SDK-side quick mitigation: JS SDK can ignore any events after a [DONE] until the next connection is established. it's a bit of hair but avoids throwing.

alex: that's what we did in the build preview and it stops the crash. but we should decide parity: do we implement the same guard in python/go SDKs?

tara: i'd prefer addressing it in the proxy/runtime long-term. short-term, we should add the client guard to all official SDKs and a test in the sampleapp. create a ticket?

omar: +1. i'll also add a small e2e test that toggles Nagle/flush to reproduce.

ci-bot: Issue opened: #4820 - "sampleapp: late SSE chunk after [DONE] on rapid reconnect (repro via proxy flush)" (reported by omar)

nina: we should also include a note in the onboarding README: "If you do extremely fast reconnects, intermediaries may replay buffered chunks resulting in late events. SDKs ignore stray events after [DONE]."

alex: sounds good. i'll send a tiny PR to the JS SDK and the sampleapp test. tagging @eng-runtime to look at proxy/tcp flags for a permanent fix.

tara: thanks. small followups: add telemetry when clients drop a post-DONE event so we can measure frequency, and update SDK changelogs.

omar: i'll handle telemetry + e2e.

alex: thanks everyone. saved a bunch of onboarding confusion already.
